sommaire.ia: AI: where it helps, where to check it

collection.heading: A fashion photo is judged at the scale of the collection
collection.p1: On a category page, items are displayed side by side. The Nielsen Norman Group observes that consistent images, with the same background, orientation, lighting and scale, are easy to scan and compare. In fashion, a difference in lighting or framing stands out all the more because the pieces look alike: two sweaters in the same knit should not look like two different shades.
collection.p2: This consistency also has to hold over time. Restocks, new colorways and the next collection will be photographed weeks or months later, sometimes by someone else. For them to sit alongside the images already online without a visible break, the lighting, angles and framing must be reproducible.
collection.p3: This is the first benefit of an automated studio for fashion: the lighting settings, the sequence of angles and the processing are saved in a template, then recalled for every piece in the same product family. Consistency then relies on the saved template rather than on settings redone at every session.

The photo must show the item actually being sold, which is also what Amazon and Google Merchant Center require in their guidelines. This is the other benefit of studio photography: showing the real product, its textures and its drape, rather than an interpretation.

tombe.texte: Laid flat, the drape can only be guessed; on a mannequin, the garment regains its shape; on a model, it shows the cut in motion and on a body. The presentation you choose determines what the customer will be able to judge.

recolo.texte: Producing the other colorways by recoloring the photo of a single item can help out occasionally. But a recolored image is not a photo of the real colorway: the exact shade, the texture and the way the fabric reacts to light may differ. interne.heading: Why photograph your collections in-house?
interne.intro: A photographer or an external studio produces polished images, especially for campaigns and editorial series. In-house production makes most sense when pieces arrive continuously and need to go online quickly.

temps.texte: Shooting templates stay in the company: the next collection is photographed under the same conditions as the previous one, even if the operator changes.

volume.texte: When styles and colorways number in the hundreds, redoing the settings at every session takes time and increases the risk of differences between images. A saved template, recalled for each piece, avoids redoing them. The volume at which in-house production pays off depends on your collections: estimate it with your own figures.

prestataire.titre: What can stay with an external provider
prestataire.texte: Campaigns, lookbooks, outdoor shoots or elaborate staging: these one-off productions can stay with a photographer or a studio. A mixed setup is possible: catalog packshots in-house, campaigns outsourced.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions about fashion packshots

q1.question: Should clothes be photographed flat, on a mannequin or on a model?
q1.answer: It depends on what the buyer needs to judge. Flat, the photo shows the shape and the prints; on a mannequin, the volume and the cut; on a model, the drape in context and the relative size. A single catalog can combine these presentations: on-model for key pieces, flat or on a mannequin for the rest. Each requires its own preparation and, often, a different studio.

q2.question: How do you get accurate colors in clothing photos?
q2.answer: By setting the lighting and camera settings for each product family, then recalling them at every shoot instead of redoing them. Difficult shades (blacks, whites, saturated colors) and shiny fabrics are checked on screen by comparing the image with the piece. Amazon and Google Merchant Center require the image to show the product actually sold, in its real color.

q3.question: Can a mannequin or a live model be photographed in an automated studio?
q3.answer: Yes, with a studio sized for it. Orbitvu designs the Alphastudio XXL for mannequins, live models and large objects (190 × 90 × 100 cm and 100 kg maximum according to the Orbitvu product sheet). The Fashion Studio is designed for on-model photography with a live model, on a dedicated stage area. Alphashot studios, such as the Alphashot XL G2 (60 × 40 × 70 cm), are sized for accessories and objects, not for a full-size mannequin or a model.

q4.question: Which studio should you use to photograph shoes and bags?
q4.answer: It depends on the size of the item. According to Orbitvu, the Alphashot XL G2 accepts products up to 60 × 40 × 70 cm and 25 kg, and the Alphashot Pro G2 up to 35 × 35 × 40 cm and 10 kg. Both shoot on a turntable, which makes it possible to run through the angles and, depending on the configuration, to produce 360° views or video.

q5.question: Can recoloring replace a photo of each colorway?
q5.answer: It can help out occasionally, but a recolored image is not a photo of the real colorway: the exact shade, the texture and the way the fabric reacts to light may differ. Photographing each real colorway shows the item actually sold. If you do recolor, compare each variant with the item before publication.

q6.question: Can AI create a ghost mannequin rendering from a flat photo?
q6.answer: Some tools offer it. The garment's volume is then generated, not photographed: check the accuracy of textures, the continuity of patterns and the legibility of printed text. These tools are evolving fast: test them on your own pieces and check every image. A real photo remains the reference for the product.

q7.question: What photos does Zalando require?
q7.answer: According to the Zalando Partner University guidelines, updated on August 31, 2026 and checked on September 28, 2026: for packshots, a white #FFFFFF background (Zalando then adds a light gray background), a portrait format with a 1:1.44 ratio, a minimum of 762 × 1,100 px and 1,801 × 2,600 px recommended, as sRGB JPEG files of up to 20 MB. Check the official page before each upload.

q8.question: How many pieces can be photographed per day?
q8.answer: No figure applies to every collection. Triggering the shot is fast; what sets the pace is preparing each piece (steaming, shaping, dressing the mannequin), the chosen presentation and the number of views. The throughput figures announced by Orbitvu are published without a measurement protocol. The most reliable approach is to test your own pieces during a demonstration.

q9.question: Do you need to be a photographer to shoot a collection in an automated studio?
q9.answer: Not for everyday packshots: according to Orbitvu, basic training is enough, with no prior photography experience. The operator prepares the pieces, chooses the saved shooting template and checks the result. For on-model shoots and campaigns, a photographer and a stylist remain valuable.

terrain.titre: Where does an automated studio really save time?
terrain.p1: Taking a photo takes less than a second. What makes producing a packshot take longer is mostly the work around it: preparing the product, repositioning it, adjusting the lighting, then processing the images and preparing the files.
terrain.p2: Unpacking, dusting, removing creases or shaping the product remains manual work. But each new angle can also require adjusting the settings again. A watch, for example, can be perfectly lit from the front. Switch to a three-quarter view without changing the light, and a reflection appears on the dial, hiding the details you wanted to show.
terrain.p3: This is where 360° rotation and saved shooting templates come into their own. With an Orbitvu automated studio, you prepare your sequence of views and its lighting settings, then save them. For products in the same family, the operator recalls this configuration: they position the product for the first view, start the sequence and let the studio run through the planned angles. Meanwhile, they can prepare the next product.
terrain.p4: The gain continues after capture. AI tools have made some retouching easier, but background removal and file preparation can still take two to three times as long as the shooting itself. Images also need to be named, margins adjusted and the dimensions required by each sales channel produced.
terrain.p5: The studio automates this sequence according to the configured profiles: background removal, cropping, size and format variants, then export to a local folder, a server or a compatible online store. The operator keeps control of the result, especially for delicate products.
terrain.p6: In practice, a well-organized production can reach 200 to 300 photos taken and finalized per day with an automated studio. In a self-built studio where these operations are carried out separately, going beyond 50 photos per day, processing included, is often difficult. These field benchmarks from PackshotCreator vary with the products, their preparation and the views required. They nonetheless give a measure of the possible gain: four to six times the daily volume.
terrain.p7: This time saving comes from all the handling the team no longer has to repeat for every product, every angle and every file.
terrain.attribution: Field benchmarks shared by Sébastien Jourdan, photographer and president of Sysnext (PackshotCreator).

r5.savoirFaire: The know-how stays in the company: your templates are used by the whole team and can be copied from one Orbitvu studio to another. According to Orbitvu, basic training is enough for routine packshots, with no prior photography experience.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions about e-commerce packshots

q1.question: Which Orbitvu studio should you choose for e-commerce products?
q1.answer: Start with the largest product to photograph: its dimensions and weight determine the possible range. Then come the views required (flat-lay, 360°, video), the volume to produce and the space available. The “Which studio for which products” table on this page lists the dimensions published by Orbitvu for each model, and PackshotCreator's studio selector narrows down the choice.

q2.question: How many photos do you need per product?
q2.answer: There is no ideal number: the images need to answer the shopper's questions. In practice: a main view, angles, details, a scale view, each variant and, where useful, the box contents. On Amazon, the Seller Central help recommends several images in addition to the main image, as well as a video.

q3.question: Is a white background mandatory?
q3.answer: Not everywhere. It is required for the main image on Amazon (pure white, RGB 255, 255, 255) and for packshots on Zalando. Google Merchant Center recommends it without requiring it; Shopify imposes nothing. A consistent white background remains the simplest way to publish the same files on several channels.

q4.question: When should you bring packshot production in-house?
q4.answer: There is no single threshold. In-house production makes sense when several criteria add up: a steady flow of new products, publishing as products arrive, products you prefer to keep on site, space and an operator available. A mixed setup remains possible. PackshotCreator's calculator compares the two options based on your volumes.

q5.question: How many photos can be produced per day with an automated studio?
q5.answer: According to PackshotCreator's field benchmarks, a well-organized production can reach 200 to 300 photos taken and finalized per day with an automated studio, whereas going beyond 50 photos per day, processing included, is often difficult in a self-built studio where these operations are carried out separately. These benchmarks vary with the products, their preparation and the views required; they are neither independent measurements nor a throughput commitment.

q6.question: Do you need to be a photographer to use an automated studio?
q6.answer: Not for routine packshots: Orbitvu states that basic training is enough, with no prior photography experience (for jewelry, some knowledge of photography is useful). The operator prepares the product, chooses a saved shooting template and checks the result. A photographer remains valuable for campaigns.

q7.question: Does an automated studio also produce 360° views and video?
q7.answer: Yes: according to Orbitvu, Alphashot and Alphastudio studios produce photos, 360° views and video. Amazon has not accepted new 360° images since December 14, 2023 (those already online remain displayed, unless a 3D model is added). The 360° view that Google generates from still photos is limited to merchants based in the United States.

q8.question: How do photos get to the online store, the PIM or the DAM?
q8.answer: The Orbitvu Station software exports files according to publishing profiles (dimensions, format, naming by reference) to a local folder or a server. Orbitvu modules exist for Magento 2, PrestaShop 1.7.x and WooCommerce, in a SUN version (subscription) or self-hosted; Shopify and Shopware 6 use the SUN version. Connections with a DAM, PIM or ERP are configured: attributes, barcodes, scripts or API.

q9.answer: At PackshotCreator, the indicative delivery time for an Orbitvu studio is about 10 days, not contractual. Installation and training time depends on the system and configuration. Delivery and installation are charged separately. A demonstration is possible beforehand, at the showroom near Lyon or by video call.

factors.heading: What influences the price of an automated photo studio
factors.body: The budget for an automated photo studio depends on four main factors. Each of them determines the right machine and therefore the final investment.
factors.f1: The size of your products: a perfume bottle and a sofa do not require the same studio. Compact machines handle products up to 40 cm, while large-format systems accommodate furniture up to 3 meters.
factors.f2: Production volume: 500 photos per year or 50,000? Your daily volume determines the level of automation needed and therefore your position in the range.
factors.f3: Types of visuals: white-background packshot, interactive 360 view, product video, textile flat-lay, ghost mannequin... Each format requires specific capabilities.
factors.f4: Level of automation desired: from a semi-automatic studio with manual adjustments to a fully automated system, the level of automation affects the price.

hero.title: Automated Studio + AI vs Pure Generative AI: the real match
hero.subtitle: Photoroom, Claid, Flair… or an Orbitvu studio combined with BlendAI.studio? The criteria for choosing.

intro.heading: Product photography is shifting to AI
intro.body1: AI has become established in product photography: many tools promise faster, cheaper visuals.
intro.body2: Two approaches coexist. On one side, generative AI tools (Photoroom, Claid, Flair, Pebblely…) that generate or transform your visuals from a photo, sometimes a basic one. On the other, the hybrid approach: an automated photo studio captures the real product, then AI derives variations from these captures. The goal is the same, professional product visuals faster; the results differ.

marketOverview.heading: The rise of generative AI for product photography
marketOverview.body1: We do not reproduce these vendors' audience, valuation or usage figures here, without a verified source.

aiPure.heading: How pure generative AI works -- and where it excels
aiPure.body1: The principle is simple. You upload a photo of your product. The tool removes the background, adjusts the lighting, generates a scene and exports a ready-to-publish visual, quickly.
aiPure.body2: For background removal or lifestyle visuals for social media and advertising, these tools can be enough, especially for simple products.
aiPure.limitesHeading: The limits of pure generative AI
aiPure.limites1: Beyond these use cases, several limits should be checked on your own products.
aiPure.limites2: A generative tool does not know your product: it can add details, distort proportions or make details disappear. Check every visual.
aiPure.limites3: Difficult materials (jewelry, transparent packaging, text, fine textures) are the most exposed to rendering errors.
aiPure.limites4: Each generation is independent: across a catalog, lighting and framing can vary from one visual to the next. Templates shared by many users also limit differentiation.
aiPure.limites5: A 360° view reconstructed from a single image remains a reconstruction, not a real shot. Check the formats offered with each vendor.
aiPure.limites6: A misleading representation of a product can expose you to sanctions from platforms and authorities. The rules applicable to AI-generated visuals are evolving: check them for your markets.

studioPlusIa.heading: Photo Studio + AI: capture reality, enhance with AI
studioPlusIa.body1: The hybrid approach starts from a different principle. The automated studio (here, an Orbitvu) captures the real product: controlled lighting, precise angle, motorized turntable. The result: a photograph of the product, in 3 seconds, with automatic background removal.
studioPlusIa.body2: AI then comes in to derive lifestyle variations from the packshot, for example with BlendAI.studio. The principle: AI creates the setting around the photographed product; product fidelity is checked on every visual. The professional defines their styles and art direction.
studioPlusIa.body3: The difference: the product displayed is a photograph, not a generated approximation. Depending on the model, the studio also enables interactive 360° views, product video, ghost mannequin or focus stacking.
studioPlusIa.body4: In terms of consistency, an automated studio reproduces the same settings from one product to the next: same lighting, same background, same framing.

whoNeedsAiPure.heading: Who should use pure generative AI
whoNeedsAiPure.body1: If your volumes are low, if your visuals are for social media or advertising, and if your products are not in a regulated sector, a generative AI tool may be enough.
whoNeedsAiPure.body2: For a reseller photographing a few items a week, such a tool can be a rational choice.
whoNeedsAiPure.body3: Nor is it a question of absolute quality. For prototypes, market research visuals, internal presentations or advertising A/B tests, generative AI can be enough and offers a speed advantage.

whoNeedsStudio.heading: Who needs a studio + AI
whoNeedsStudio.body1: The equation changes as soon as any of these criteria come into play.
whoNeedsStudio.criteria1detail: As volumes increase, consistency becomes critical. An Orbitvu studio produces 200 to 300 packshots per day. Return on investment is usually between 6 and 12 months depending on volume, with no guarantee.
whoNeedsStudio.criteria2detail: When a professional buyer orders technical parts from a catalog, they need to see the exact product, not an interpretation. Luxury and technical products require an exact representation: that is what a photograph of the real product provides.
whoNeedsStudio.criteria3detail: Medical, defense, industry: depending on the sector, visuals must be traceable and verifiable. A real photograph, with its metadata, makes this traceability easier.
whoNeedsStudio.criteria4detail: If your product pages need interactive 360°, video, ghost mannequin or focus stacking, an automated studio with a turntable produces real shots from several angles.
whoNeedsStudio.criteria5detail: With shared templates, differentiation is limited. Defining your own styles and art direction lets you assert your brand identity.
whoNeedsStudio.body2: The upfront investment is higher (starting at EUR 12,450 for an Alphashot 360, or EUR 270/month on a 60-month lease). Return on investment is usually between 6 and 12 months depending on volume, with no guarantee.

q1.question: Will AI replace photo studios?
q1.answer: No. Generative AI suits background removal, lifestyle scenes and quick tests, but it does not capture the real product. For capture, 360° and catalog consistency, an automated studio provides a real shot; AI can then derive variations of the visuals.

q2.question: Is Photoroom enough for an e-commerce site?
q2.answer: It depends on the context. For low volumes, simple products and limited fidelity requirements, a tool like Photoroom may be enough. For a B2B catalog, luxury or regulated sectors, fidelity and consistency become decisive: compare on your own products.

q3.question: What is BlendAI.studio?
q3.answer: BlendAI.studio is an AI product photography tool presented on this site. It starts from a professional packshot and generates lifestyle variations, backgrounds and retouching; product fidelity is checked on every visual. For terms, contact us.

q4.question: Can generative AI produce 360 views?
q4.answer: Some tools generate approximations of 360° views from a single image: these are reconstructions, not real multi-angle views. An automated studio with a turntable produces real shots from several angles. Check the formats offered with each vendor.

q5.question: What budget to start with a studio + AI?
q5.answer: The Alphashot 360 (entry-level) starts at EUR 12,450 excl. VAT, or EUR 270/month on a 60-month lease, an estimate to be confirmed by our sales team. Return on investment is usually between 6 and 12 months depending on volume, with no guarantee. For BlendAI.studio, contact us.

q6.question: Are AI visuals legal for e-commerce?
q6.answer: Yes, provided they do not mislead about the product. The rules applicable to AI-generated visuals (labeling, rights, product representation) vary across countries and platforms and are evolving: check them for your markets and sector.

hero.title: Outsource vs in-house product photography

intro.heading: PackshotCreator is not a photo service provider
intro.p1: We get this question all the time: can you photograph our products? The answer is no. PackshotCreator does not offer photo services. We sell Orbitvu automated photo studio systems and train your teams to use them.
intro.p2: This confusion is telling. It shows that many businesses have not yet realised there is an alternative between "outsource everything" and "hire a photographer". This article helps you compare both approaches with concrete figures.
intro.p3: Spoiler: both options have their place. But beyond a certain volume, one becomes clearly more advantageous.

whenOutsource.heading: When outsourcing makes sense
whenOutsource.p1: Outsourcing product photography remains a perfectly valid option in several situations. If your catalogue does not exceed 500 photos per year, if you have no immediate investment budget, if your need is occasional or seasonal, or if you simply lack the space for a studio, a service provider is the pragmatic solution.
whenOutsource.p2: A competent provider delivers professional visuals without requiring you to master anything. You send your products, you get back images that meet your specifications.
whenOutsource.p3: In terms of pricing, expect between 19 and 50 euros (excl. VAT) per standard packshot in France. Packages are available: around 149 euros for 10 photos (including one hour of shooting, one hour of preparation, and two hours of retouching). For large volumes over 100 photos, some providers go as low as 5 euros per photo.

prices.volume: From EUR 5 excl. VAT / photo (> 100 photos)

whenInternalize.heading: When bringing it in-house becomes obvious
whenInternalize.p1: The tipping point generally sits around 500 photos per year. Beyond that threshold, the cumulative cost of outsourcing starts to exceed the total cost of ownership of an automated studio.
whenInternalize.p2: But volume is not the only criterion. Bringing photography in-house becomes a natural choice when:

reasons.r1: Your time-to-market is critical and every day of delay costs you sales
reasons.r2: You need absolute visual consistency across all your products
reasons.r3: Product photography is a strategic skill you want to build internally
reasons.r4: Your volume is growing and outsourcing costs are rising proportionally

whenInternalize.p3: The rule is simple: when the annual cost of your service provider exceeds the total cost of ownership of a studio (purchase amortised over 5 years + consumables + operator time), it is time to switch.

trapsPrestataire.heading: The pitfalls of outsourcing
trapsPrestataire.p1: Outsourcing is not without risks, and those risks grow with volume.

t1.title: Lead times
t1.description: Count on an average of three weeks between sending your products and receiving the visuals. For a product launch, that is an eternity.

t2.title: Visual inconsistency
t2.description: From one shoot to the next, conditions change. Different lighting, different photographer, different retouching. Your catalogue loses its coherence.

t3.title: Dependency
t3.description: The expertise stays with the provider, not with you. If they raise prices, change methods, or close shop, you are back to square one.

t4.title: Costs proportional to volume
t4.description: The more you grow, the more you pay. Outsourcing is a variable cost that offers no economies of scale on the client side.

gainsInternal.heading: What you gain by bringing it in-house
gainsInternal.p1: An automated Orbitvu studio does not require a professional photographer. After one hour of hands-on practice, any team member can produce calibrated, repeatable packshots.

g1.title: Total control
g1.description: Lighting, angle, background, framing: you define your standards once, and the system reproduces them identically.

g2.title: Speed
g2.description: 3 seconds per packshot. Up to 300 photos per day per operator, compared with 30 using a traditional photographer.

g3.title: Consistent quality
g3.description: Settings are saved in templates. The 10,000th packshot is identical to the first.

g4.title: Independence
g4.description: The expertise stays within your company. You no longer depend on anyone.

g5.title: Instant scaling
g5.description: New catalogue, seasonal collection, client emergency: you produce when you need to, not when the provider is available.

g6.title: Rich content
g6.description: Beyond simple packshots, an Orbitvu studio produces 360-degree views, videos, and AI-ready content (BlendAI).

ourTake.heading: Why we chose Orbitvu
ourTake.transparencyNote: Transparency disclaimer: PackshotCreator is the official Orbitvu distributor in France. The arguments below reflect our conviction, based on our field experience and available factual data.
ourTake.body1: We chose to distribute Orbitvu for France and Switzerland. Here are our reasons:
ourTake.reason1: 78 visual contents per day with the Alphashot XL PRO V2, versus 33 with Ortery's 3D PhotoBench 280 (study carried out in 2023 at PackshotCreator's request).
ourTake.reason2: According to the author of the 2023 study, Orbitvu Station proved more intuitive than the Ortery software.
ourTake.reason3: 16 systems covering everything from 18 cm jewelry to 2.5 m furniture. The French market is diverse: luxury, cosmetics, fashion, industry, food.
ourTake.reason4: Sales, installation (charged extra), training (billed separately; Sysnext is Qualiopi-certified) and technical support in French.
ourTake.fairness: The right choice depends on your context: compare the manufacturers' offers on your own products.

q1.question: Are you objective in this comparison?
q1.answer: We are the official Orbitvu distributor in France and Switzerland, and we say so clearly. q2.question: Is Ortery cheaper than Orbitvu?
q2.answer: We do not publish price comparisons. Orbitvu is offered on quote, depending on the configuration; for Ortery, please check with the manufacturer.

q3.question: Is Styleshoots suited to fashion?
q3.answer: We do not detail the StyleShoots offer, without a verified source. Orbitvu covers fashion with the Alphastudio XXL and the Fashion Studio Pro, as well as other sectors (footwear, accessories, cosmetics, furniture). Compare the solutions on your own products.

q4.question: What is the productivity difference between Orbitvu and Ortery?
q4.answer: According to the study carried out in 2023 at PackshotCreator's request, Orbitvu's Alphashot XL PRO V2 produces 78 visual contents per day versus 33 for Ortery's 3D PhotoBench 280 (theoretical calculation at 100% utilization), a 2.4x gap. For a 3D animation with 48 photos: 369 seconds versus 1,521 seconds.

q5.question: Who provides after-sales support in France for each brand?
q5.answer: Orbitvu: PackshotCreator (Sysnext company), with showroom, training (Sysnext is Qualiopi-certified) and French-language technical support. For other brands, please check with the manufacturers.

q6.question: Can you test the solutions before buying?
q6.answer: PackshotCreator offers Orbitvu demonstrations at its showroom in Beynost, near Lyon, by appointment; other arrangements can be agreed. Contact us to schedule a test with your own products.
